title: A Hayride Through the Farm
description: Ride behind the tractor in a wagon with straw-covered seats.
cardDescription: Ride behind the tractor in a wagon with straw-covered seats.
focus: The setting is a Hayride Through the Farm. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Outing on a farm wagon with hay bales
Dry stems used for animal bedding
Powered farm vehicle that can pull equipment
Round part that turns on an axle
Farm building for animals or hay
Place for one person to sit
Tightly packed bundle of hay or straw
Travel on a vehicle or amusement attraction
Marked strip of pool space used by a swimmer

answerNotes.WAGON: A wagon carries people or goods on wheels. A hayride uses the vehicle for an outing, with straw or hay providing the familiar farm setting.
answerNotes.HAY: Hay is cut vegetation dried for animal feed. Straw is mainly the dry stalks left after a grain crop is harvested.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.BARN: A barn is a farm building. Its uses can include sheltering animals and storing hay, equipment, or crops.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.

answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.WAGON: A wagon carries people or goods on wheels. A hayride uses the vehicle for an outing, with straw or hay providing the familiar farm setting.
answerNotes.PICK: Pick can mean choose or pluck. In a harvest setting, it usually means gathering something from the plant.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.

To break an ingredient into smaller pieces by pressure
Sweet produce such as an apple

answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.BARREL: A barrel is a large rounded container. A rain barrel collects runoff; its tap lets water leave without lifting the whole container.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.

answerNotes.STITCH: A stitch is one unit of worked thread or yarn. Many stitches together form a seam, knitted row, or decorative pattern.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.PATTERN: A pattern is an arrangement that repeats. In sewing, the same word can also mean a template for cutting fabric pieces.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.BARN: A barn is a farm building. Its uses can include sheltering animals and storing hay, equipment, or crops.

answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
